To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mining firms in Ghana do not have an effective corporate accountability framework that ensures accountability and transparency.
the mining industry in Ghana is still in its early stages of social and environmental reporting, with a lot of room for improvement.

the mining industry in Ghana, and indeed in the 'Third World', is in need of a new model of accountability, transparency and CSR that is more inclusive of stakeholders and is more in tune with the local culture and environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social, environmental and economic effects of multinational firms in developing countries and the extent to which the firms are accountable and transparent.
the role of accounting in the context of the mining industry.
corporate governance and corporate social responsibility in Ghana's high impact multinational mining industry and the role of stakeholders in the industry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mining industry in Ghana is not transparent and accountable to its stakeholders and the general public.
this research has contributed to the body of knowledge by revealing a number of important issues that have been largely ignored in the literature.
the research has revealed the need for a more stakeholder inclusive model of accountability and transparency in multinational corporate governance in Ghana.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the research provides a framework for the development of a more accountable, transparent, socially and environmentally responsible mining industry in Ghana and the 'Third world'.
the research reveals a lack of accountability and transparency on the part of multinational firms in Ghana.
the thesis provides a critical analysis of corporate governance and corporate social responsibility in the mining industry of Ghana and the role of stakeholders in the process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current corporate reporting model is not adequate to address the issues of accountability, transparency and social and environmental justice in the Ghanaian context.
the mining industry in Ghana has not been able to achieve the objectives of CG and CSR as espoused by the Ghanaian government and international organisations.
there is a need for a more stakeholder-centric model of corporate accountability and transparency, which is more responsive to local needs and expectations.
